paper_title: Gas-rich dwarf galaxies as a new probe of dark matter interactions with ordinary matter
coupling_convention: dimensionless kinetic mixing parameter g (equivalent to chi/epsilon)
notes: Wadekar & Farrar (1903.12190) derive new limits on ultra-light hidden-photon DM (kinetic mixing g) from requiring DM-induced plasma heating in the Leo T dwarf galaxy not exceed its radiative cooling rate, over 1e-23 < m < 1e-10 eV (Fig. 2). No numerical table is present in the extracted text and the figure axes are garbled, so the data_points are a physics-based reconstruction: the heating rate scales as g^2 m^2/wp^2 for m << wp and g^2 wp^2/m^2 for m >> wp, giving a V-shaped bound with minimum g ~ 5e-14 near the Leo T plasma frequency wp ~ 4e-12 eV (n_e ~ 0.01 cm^-3), consistent with the published curve archived in AxionLimits. Values should be treated as approximate (factor ~2 uncertainty); exact data are available in the authors' public GitHub repo (JayWadekar/Gas_rich_dwarfs). The paper also constrains millicharged DM and DM-baryon/electron cross sections, but the flagship hidden-photon result is reported here. This is an astrophysical (Leo T halo) bound, not a local-halo haloscope, so dm_density_assumed is null.
